newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan approves bill to allow organ transplants.
newsitem.headline: Japan approves bill to allow organ transplants.

text.p: Japan's parliament on Thursday passed a bill recognising an end of brain functions as legal death, clearing the way for organ transplants in the country for the first time since a 1968 heart transplant sparked criminal investigations.
The bill was approved 320-148 in the 500-seat Lower House of parliament.
The bill would allow organ transplants from those declared brain dead provided the donor provides written consent in advance. Previous practice held that cardiac arrest defined death.
Doctors have shied away from performing organ transplants since a landmark 1968 heart transplant from a brain dead donor resulted in a 15-month criminal investigation. No charges were ever filed.
Unable to receive organ donations at home, about 170 Japanese have gone abroad to receive heart and liver transplants, according to an organ recipients group.
